title: DevSecOps CI/CD Pipeline with SAST, SCA & Container Admission Gates
problem: Software vulnerabilities introduced during feature development become exponentially costlier to remediate once deployed into production environments. Modern software engineering requires automated security gates embedded directly into CI/CD pipelines to intercept security flaws before code merge. This project constructs an automated DevSecOps pipeline using GitHub Actions, Semgrep, Trivy, and Cosign. The system enforces strict static application security testing (SAST), software composition analysis (SCA) for known CVEs, secrets leakage detection, container image vulnerability scanning, and cryptographic artifact signing with automated build failure policies.
use_cases: Enterprise CI/CD quality gates enforcing SOC2 and PCI-DSS application security standards
Automated dependency audit workflows blocking vulnerable open-source packages in pull requests
Supply chain security pipelines cryptographically signing container images prior to production deployment
hard_parts: Tuning SAST rules to eliminate developer false positives while maintaining high recall on critical flaws
Managing software composition analysis vulnerability thresholds across transitive dependency trees
Implementing cryptographic container signing with Cosign keyless infrastructure and admission verification
Designing fail-fast pipeline gating logic that delivers actionable remediation reports without stalling build velocity
screener_signals: Modular GitHub Actions workflow configurations cleanly separating SAST, SCA, container scanning, and signing
Automated vulnerability test suite with intentional defect fixtures confirming pipeline blocking enforcement
Anti-fake verification script injecting dynamic secret tokens and high-severity CVEs into test PRs to assert blocking

components.name: SAST DevSecOps Static Code Scanner
components.purpose: Scans application source code for injection vulnerabilities, insecure cryptosystems, and leaked tokens

components.name: SCA Dependency & Secrets Auditor
components.purpose: Audits third-party dependency manifests against known CVE databases and generates CycloneDX SBOMs

components.name: Container Vulnerability Scanner
components.purpose: Inspects container base images and filesystem packages for high and critical CVE vulnerabilities

components.name: Cryptographic Image Signer & Policy Gate
components.purpose: Signs clean container digests cryptographically and rejects unsigned or vulnerable container artifacts

architecture.data_flow: Pull requests trigger GitHub Actions; Semgrep parses source files for code vulnerabilities and secret keys; Trivy analyzes project lockfiles for known dependency CVEs and generates an SBOM; Docker builds the container image; Trivy executes a deep filesystem scan on the container; if critical CVEs or secrets are detected, the pipeline terminates with exit code 1; if clean, Cosign cryptographically signs the image digest and generates an attestation log.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: GitHub Actions status checks blocking branch merges; Cosign signature verification rejecting unsigned container admission.

prerequisites: Familiarity with Git branching, pull request workflows, and CI/CD concepts
Basic knowledge of Docker containerization, shell scripting, and application security principles (OWASP Top 10)

environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source software stack on free GitHub public repositories or local runners)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: Free GitHub account for Actions, or local Act runner without cloud dependencies
environment.reference_environment: Ubuntu 22.04 with Docker 24+, Semgrep CLI, and Trivy CLI installed
environment.fallback_path: Local command-line script running Semgrep and Trivy directly without GitHub Actions

riskiest_component.name: Pipeline Flakiness from Upstream CVE Database Rate Limiting
riskiest_component.fallback: Cache Trivy vulnerability database locally in runner cache to decouple scanning from network rate limits

deliverables: Git repository containing GitHub Actions workflow definitions (.github/workflows/sec-pipeline.yml)
Custom Semgrep rule configuration YAML files targeting insecure application patterns
Automated vulnerability test harness verifying pipeline failure on dirty code branches
Screener verification script executing security scanners and dynamic defect check in under 2 minutes
out_of_scope: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) with active network fuzzing
Full-scale runtime cloud security posture management (CSPM)
Manual penetration testing reporting and remediation consulting
safety_note: This project executes automated security vulnerability scanners and static analysis tools on local test repositories. It does not perform active network penetration, unauthorized port scanning, or malicious exploitation against external computing systems.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an automated DevSecOps CI/CD pipeline with Semgrep SAST, Trivy SCA and container scanning, Cosign signing, and blocking gates.
worksheet.q2: Target users: DevSecOps engineers, security platform architects, and CI/CD infrastructure teams.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: enterprise SOC2 compliance gates, automated dependency CVE audits, and container supply chain signing.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: SAST rule false-positive tuning, SCA transitive dependency management, Cosign keyless container signing, and fail-fast pipeline gating.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 10,000 LOC microservice with planted vulnerabilities. Mock synthetic credentials only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, free GitHub public repo. Fallback: local CLI scanning without GitHub Actions.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Upstream CVE database rate limiting. Fallback: local runner caching of vulnerability databases.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded green build logs. Anti-fake check 5 injects dynamic secret at runtime and asserts blocking gate failure.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; automated local vulnerability scanners only, no unauthorized external network penetration.
